interpretations.headline: Notice what happens between instructions and action
interpretations.summary: When a class starts a group task, students may need to collect materials, read an example, and complete a first step. A student might handle each instruction separately yet lose track of the order when several are given together. This score averages nine observations about keeping track of directions, steps, and plans. A higher mean indicates that more of these difficulties matched what you observed.

guidance.text: Choose one familiar lesson task. Record which directions the student acted on, where they asked for a repeat, and what was happening in the class at that point.
Try posting the first two steps or leaving an example in view for the whole class. Observe whether the student can resume the task after a brief interruption.

interpretations.headline: Look at the handoff between activities
interpretations.summary: After an energetic group discussion, a student may keep talking while the class moves to individual work. The same student may switch more smoothly when there is a clear signal for what comes next. This score averages eleven observations about pausing responses, ending preferred activities, and starting or finishing tasks. A higher mean indicates that more of these difficulties matched your observations.

guidance.text: Compare two class transitions or work periods. Note the activity, the cue you gave, and what the student did next. Include a situation where the switch went smoothly.
Try one consistent cue for the next transition and make the first step visible. Observe whether starting becomes easier in that classroom setting.

interpretations.headline: Use the two subscale means to understand the details
interpretations.summary: This summary averages all 20 responses, including nine working-memory items and eleven inhibition items. The same overall mean can describe different classroom patterns. Use the two subscales and your own observations to identify a setting worth looking at more closely.

guidance.text: Write a short note about one classroom situation you observed. Leave room for the student or another observer to describe what happened from their perspective.

limitations: The two subscale means summarise what you reported as the teacher observer. They describe the settings you have seen. The original 2020 study evaluated adolescent self-ratings and parent observations.

Scores use the existing 1–5 response scale. The Working Memory and Inhibition means are the two published subscale results. The overall item mean is a Huisurvey descriptive summary. This pilot does not apply norms, score bands, or thresholds.
Use this English observer form for teenagers ages 13–19. Parent, teacher, and self-reports reflect different perspectives and should be considered separately.

Source: Thorell, Lazarević, Milovanović, and Bugarski Ignjatović (2020), Teenage Executive Functioning Inventory (TEXI), https://doi.org/10.1080/09297049.2020.1726885. English observer form and scoring guide: https://www.chexi.se/.
report.disclaimer: This pilot report is for describing observations and reviewing everyday support. Please do not use these results for diagnosis, ranking, disciplinary decisions, or school placement.
